steps.name: Build the line
steps.narration: A number line is a ruler for numbers: equal gaps, every whole number gets its own line, and it keeps going both ways.
steps.prompt: Are the gaps between the numbers equal?

steps.name: Place a point
steps.narration: Seven is seven equal steps from zero. The ring marks exactly where it sits.

steps.name: Negatives
steps.narration: To the left of zero the numbers are negative. Minus four is four steps left of zero, so it is smaller than minus one.

steps.name: Decimals
steps.narration: Zoom into 0 to 1 and split it into ten equal parts. Each line is one tenth, so the ring is at 0.6.

steps.name: Compare
steps.narration: Two lines, one scale. Minus six is further left than minus two, so minus six is less than minus two.

steps.name: Thermometer
steps.narration: Stand the line up and it becomes a thermometer. From minus five degrees, a rise of eight takes us to three degrees.

steps.name: Big numbers
steps.narration: The same line works for thousands. Each line is two thousand, so this point is six thousand seven hundred and fifty.

steps.name: Whole numbers
steps.narration: Here is 0 to 10. Our number, 3.47, is somewhere between 3 and 4, but at this zoom we cannot see exactly where.
steps.prompt: Which two whole numbers is 3.47 between?

steps.name: Zoom to tenths
steps.narration: Zoom into the gap from 3 to 4 and split it into ten equal parts. Each line is now one tenth. 3.47 sits between 3.4 and 3.5.
steps.prompt: How many tenths are between 3 and 4?

steps.name: Zoom to hundredths
steps.narration: Zoom again: 3.4 to 3.5 splits into ten hundredths. Now we can see it exactly: 3.47.

steps.name: Times ten
steps.narration: Every zoom makes the gap ten times smaller: ones, then tenths, then hundredths. That is place value on a line.

steps.name: Negatives
steps.narration: Zoom works below zero too. Minus 0.35 is between minus 0.4 and minus 0.3, exactly halfway.

steps.name: Thousandths
steps.narration: Start at 0 to 1 in tenths and zoom twice: 0.125 is one hundred and twenty-five thousandths.

steps.name: Start
steps.narration: Every jump sum starts with a ring on the start number. Here we start at minus three.

steps.name: Jump on
steps.narration: Adding means jumping right. Minus three add five: jump five to the right, crossing zero, and land on two.

steps.name: Jump back
steps.narration: Subtracting means jumping left. Seven take away nine: jump nine to the left and land on minus two.

steps.name: Friendly jumps
steps.narration: Big jumps can be split. Forty-eight add twenty-seven: two to fifty, then twenty to seventy, then five to seventy-five.

steps.name: Repeated jumps
steps.narration: Four jumps of three from zero land on twelve. Multiplication is repeated equal jumps.

steps.name: Subtract a negative
steps.narration: Taking away minus three is the same as adding three: four take away minus three is seven. Two minus signs make a jump to the right.

steps.name: Decimals
steps.narration: Jumps work with decimals too. Two point six add point seven: point four to three, then point three more. Three point three.

steps.name: Landmarks
steps.narration: To round 37 to the nearest ten, find the tens either side: 30 and 40. They are the landmarks at the bottom of the hill.

steps.name: Halfway hill
steps.narration: The top of the hill is halfway, 35. A ball on the hill always rolls down to the nearer landmark.

steps.name: Roll
steps.narration: 37 is past the top, on the 40 side, so the ball rolls to 40. 37 rounded to the nearest ten is 40.

steps.name: Exactly halfway
steps.narration: What about 35, right on the top? The rule is: halfway rounds up. So 35 rounds to 40.

steps.name: Decimals
steps.narration: To one decimal place, the landmarks are tenths. 4.63 is between 4.6 and 4.7; halfway is 4.65, so it rolls back to 4.6.

steps.name: Hundreds
steps.narration: 6748 to the nearest hundred: the landmarks are 6700 and 6800, halfway is 6750. 6748 is just short of the top, so it rolls to 6700.

steps.name: Negatives
steps.narration: Negatives work the same way. Minus 23 is between minus 30 and minus 20, nearer minus 20, so it rounds to minus 20.

steps.name: Greater than
steps.narration: x is greater than 2 means every number to the right of 2. The open ring says 2 itself is not included.

steps.name: Or equal to
steps.narration: Add a line under the sign and 2 joins in: x is greater than or equal to 2. The ring is filled in.
steps.prompt: What changed from the last line?

steps.name: Less than
steps.narration: x is less than minus 1 points left: minus 2, minus 3 and every number in between, but not minus 1 itself.

steps.name: Between
steps.narration: Two signs make a segment. Minus 2 is less than x, and x is at most 3: open at minus 2, filled at 3.

steps.name: Integer solutions
steps.narration: If x must be a whole number, list the integers on the segment: minus 1, 0, 1, 2 and 3. Five integers.
steps.prompt: Why is −2 not in the list?

steps.name: Decimals
steps.narration: Solutions are not only whole numbers. x is at least 1.5, so 1.5, 1.8 and 2.75 all work.

steps.name: The line
steps.narration: Here is a line from minus 5 to 5 with a line at every whole number. Each card goes where its number lives.

steps.name: First card
steps.narration: Minus 3 is three steps left of zero. Place the card, and its stem points to the spot.

steps.name: More cards
steps.narration: 2 goes right of zero, and minus 0.5 sits halfway between minus 1 and 0.

steps.name: All placed
steps.narration: Now 4 and 0. Read the cards from left to right and they are in order, smallest first.

steps.name: Decimals
steps.narration: With decimals, look at the tenths. 0.05 is less than 0.3 even though it has more digits.

steps.name: Estimate
steps.narration: With only tens marked, estimate. 68 is just before 70; 7 is close to 0.

steps.name: The question
steps.narration: Estimate 49 times 21. We do not need the exact answer, just a sensible size.

steps.name: Round each
steps.narration: Round each number to one significant figure: 49 is about 50 and 21 is about 20.

steps.name: Estimate
steps.narration: 50 times 20 is 1000. The estimate ring goes at 1000 on the line.

steps.name: Check
steps.narration: The exact answer is 1029. The bracket shows the estimate was very close, so the answer is sensible.
steps.prompt: How far was the estimate from 1029?

steps.name: Decimals
steps.narration: 3.87 times 19.6: round to 4 times 20, which is 80. The exact answer is 75.852.

steps.name: Square roots
steps.narration: Square root of 50 is not a whole number. 49 is 7 squared and 64 is 8 squared, so root 50 is just over 7. It is irrational: the decimal never ends.
steps.prompt: Which two whole numbers is √50 between?

steps.narration: This scale has numbers every 20 kilograms. Before reading it, find out what each small mark is worth.

steps.name: Each division
steps.narration: 20 split into 5 gaps: 20 divided by 5 is 4. Each small division is 4 kilograms.

steps.name: Read
steps.narration: The pointer is two divisions past 60. 60 plus 4 plus 4 is 68 kilograms.

steps.name: Jug
steps.narration: The jug is labelled every 100 millilitres with 5 gaps, so each is 20. The water is two marks above 300: 340 millilitres.
steps.prompt: What is each mark on the jug worth?

steps.name: Dial
steps.narration: A round dial works the same way. Labels go up in 2s with 4 gaps, so each mark is 0.5 kilograms. The needle is one mark past 6: 6.5 kilograms.
steps.prompt: What is each mark on the dial worth?

steps.name: Negative scale
steps.narration: Thermometers go below zero. Each mark is 2 degrees, and the level is three marks below zero: minus 6.
steps.prompt: Is the level above or below 0?

steps.name: Error interval
steps.narration: A length of 7.3 centimetres to one decimal place could be anything from 7.25 up to, but not including, 7.35.

steps.name: Powers line
steps.narration: Each mark on this line is ten times the one before: 1, 10, 100, 1000 and so on. The small raised number is the power of ten.

steps.name: Between powers
steps.narration: 320 thousand is more than 100 thousand but less than a million, so it sits between 10 to the 5 and 10 to the 6.

steps.name: Zoom in
steps.narration: Zoom into that gap. It is split into 1 to 10 lots of 10 to the 5. 320 thousand is 3.2 lots, so it is 3.2 times 10 to the 5.

steps.name: Compare
steps.narration: To compare, look at the power first. 3.2 times 10 to the 5 is bigger than 8 times 10 to the 4, even though 8 is bigger than 3.2.

steps.name: Small numbers
steps.narration: Small numbers use negative powers. 0.0045 is between 10 to the minus 3 and 10 to the minus 2: it is 4.5 times 10 to the minus 3.

steps.name: Huge
steps.narration: Standard form handles enormous numbers too. 6.02 times 10 to the 23 is just past the 10 to the 23 mark.

steps.name: Measured
steps.narration: A length is 7.3 centimetres to one decimal place. The real length was rounded, so it might not be exactly 7.3.
steps.prompt: Could the real length be 7.28 cm?

steps.name: Halfway marks
steps.narration: Anything from halfway down to halfway up rounds to 7.3. Halfway to 7.2 is 7.25, and halfway to 7.4 is 7.35.

steps.name: The interval
steps.narration: 7.25 rounds up to 7.3, so it is included: filled end. 7.35 would round to 7.4, so it is not included: open end.
steps.prompt: Why is the right-hand end open?

steps.name: Nearest 10
steps.narration: 340 people to the nearest 10: halfway down is 335 and halfway up is 345. So 335 is at most the number, which is less than 345.
steps.prompt: What are the halfway marks for 340?

steps.name: Truncated
steps.narration: Truncating chops off digits instead of rounding. 4.7 truncated could be anything from 4.7 up to, but not including, 4.8.

steps.name: Bounds in a calculation
steps.narration: A square has side 5 centimetres to the nearest centimetre, so the side is from 4.5 up to 5.5. The perimeter is from 4 times 4.5 equals 18, up to 4 times 5.5 equals 22.
steps.prompt: What is the upper bound of the perimeter?
